title: FOLFOX-4

agents.name: Oxaliplatin
agents.explanation: Oxaliplatin makes links within DNA. These interfere with copying and repair, which can stop a cancer cell dividing. Healthy tissues can also be affected.
agents.watch: Cold can trigger tingling or throat discomfort. Tell the team about persistent numbness, difficulty with buttons or walking, or infusion symptoms. New breathing difficulty always needs assessment.
risks: Persistent sensory neuropathy, sometimes lasting after treatment
Rare serious lung or blood complications

agents.name: Folinic acid
agents.explanation: Folinic acid helps fluorouracil remain bound to an enzyme needed to make DNA. In this regimen it increases fluorouracil activity and can also increase its unwanted effects. It is not a vitamin supplement to start yourself.
agents.watch: The combined treatment can increase mouth soreness and diarrhoea. Report these promptly. Rare allergic reactions can occur.

agents.name: Fluorouracil
agents.explanation: Fluorouracil interferes with the production and use of DNA and RNA, the instructions cells need to grow. The infusion extends exposure over approximately two days.
agents.watch: Diarrhoea, mouth sores and skin soreness may become serious. Chest pain during the pump infusion needs emergency assessment. Unexpected severe early toxicity can occur even after DPD testing.
risks: Severe early toxicity including DPD-related toxicity

sources.title: HSE: chemotherapy side effects and urgent advice

questions.a: FOLFOX-4 may be given after surgery for stage II or III colon cancer, or for colorectal cancer that has spread. Your team explains the aim, alternatives and how benefit will be reviewed.

questions.q: Do I need to enter dates to understand the cycle?
questions.a: No. The graph explains a general pattern. Your hospital arranges appointments; the guide and its safety information are available without entering anything.

questions.q: Will I have a pump at home?
questions.a: Arrange Day 2 infusion renewal and final disconnection around Day 3. This is two separate 22-hour infusions; do not use a 46-hour pump timetable.

questions.q: What happens if a dose is delayed?
questions.a: The team checks the cause and may delay, reduce, change or stop one medicine. Ask which component changes and when you should next attend; do not restart yourself.

questions.q: How will I know whether it is helping?
questions.a: Scans, symptoms and clinical review assess benefit. A rash, side effect or good day alone cannot show whether the cancer is responding.
This NCCP regimen does not contain a routine radiotherapy course. If radiation is recommended separately, ask whether it is before, during or after these medicines.

questions.q: What about fertility, pregnancy and breastfeeding?
questions.a: Discuss fertility preservation and reproductive plans before treatment. Ask for the contraception and breastfeeding instructions for every medicine; the whole regimen may require longer precautions than one medicine alone.

questions.q: Why is Day 2 different from other FOLFOX leaflets?
questions.a: NCCP FOLFOX-4 has fluorouracil on Days 1 and 2, each with a 22-hour infusion. It is not modified FOLFOX-6. The team confirms your Day 2 prescription and visit; do not rely on another FOLFOX schedule.

phases_note: This is a general explanation, not an appointment calendar. Delays or changes are decided by your team. Each medicine can need a different change.
timeline_note: NCCP defines the treatment days. Symptom bands are broad educational guidance; reactions can occur on any day, and cumulative effects may continue between cycles.
safety_note: Fever, shivers or suddenly feeling unwell require immediate contact. Serious symptoms override any timeline or diary.
teachback: Can you explain which visits are planned, whether a pump is involved, and which symptoms mean you should call today? No dates or symptom scores are needed to use this guide.
consent_support: Discuss the treatment aim, alternatives, expected benefit, serious and lasting risks, fertility/pregnancy precautions and the contact plan. Explain DPD testing and the exact pump schedule.
urgent_extra: New breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse, severe diarrhoea or inability to drink require prompt assessment. Call for line pain, swelling, leakage or unexpected pump progress.

chapters.title: Your treatment aim
chapters.intro: The setting changes what benefit means.

items.title: Why this option?
items.text: FOLFOX-4 may be given after surgery for stage II or III colon cancer, or for colorectal cancer that has spread. Your team explains the aim, alternatives and how benefit will be reviewed.

items.title: A plan that can change
items.text: Ask whether the aim is to reduce recurrence risk, control cancer, relieve symptoms or support a local treatment. Your preferences and priorities matter.

items.title: Blood tests and medicines
items.text: Review blood counts, kidney/liver tests, symptoms, allergies and all medicines and supplements. Confirm DPD testing before fluorouracil. Kidney impairment can affect uracil-based DPD testing interpretation.

items.title: Preparing access
items.text: Arrange Day 2 infusion renewal and final disconnection around Day 3. This is two separate 22-hour infusions; do not use a 46-hour pump timetable.

chapters.title: Symptoms in context
chapters.intro: Report what changed and how it affects you.

items.title: When to call
items.text: New breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse, severe diarrhoea or inability to drink require prompt assessment. Call for line pain, swelling, leakage or unexpected pump progress.

items.title: Bowel symptoms
items.text: Follow your written rescue plan. Fever, blood, severe pain, reduced urine or inability to drink needs urgent advice.

items.title: Skin or nerve changes
items.text: Avoid cold drinks and cold exposure as instructed after oxaliplatin; do not suck ice chips during fluorouracil in this regimen. Use prescribed anti-sickness medicines, pace activities and ask for nutritional, emotional or practical support.

chapters.title: Visits and treatment sequence
chapters.intro: Know which steps happen in the clinic and at home.

items.title: The exact delivery plan
items.text: Day 1: oxaliplatin and folinic acid, then fluorouracil bolus and a 22-hour infusion. Day 2: further fluorouracil bolus and a second 22-hour infusion; completion around Day 3. A repeating 14-day cycle. For adjuvant FOLFOX-4, NCCP describes 12 cycles; metastatic treatment continues while suitable.

items.title: Radiotherapy relationship
items.text: This NCCP regimen does not contain a routine radiotherapy course. If radiation is recommended separately, ask whether it is before, during or after these medicines.

items.title: Symptoms and monitoring
items.text: Persistent numbness after oxaliplatin needs follow-up. Ask which medicines to continue, when to seek help and how response will be assessed.

items.title: Next decisions
items.text: The team reviews benefit, side effects and your priorities. Supportive and palliative care can help alongside active treatment. Ask for a clear next-step and contact plan.

timeline.label: Blood counts / infection risk
timeline.text: Blood tests and symptoms guide review

day_groups.title: Treatment and checks
day_groups.body: The team reviews blood tests, symptoms and your prescription before treatment.
day_groups.action: Know the contact number and the next planned visit.

day_groups.title: Day 2 treatment and completion
day_groups.body: A second fluorouracil treatment is planned on Day 2; trained staff renew the infusion. The team confirms the setting and any other Day 2 medicines.
day_groups.action: Call early for symptoms; do not wait for the next appointment.

day_groups.title: Recovery and the next review
day_groups.body: The team uses symptoms, tests and your priorities to decide what happens next.
day_groups.action: Bring questions and a symptom record if useful; this is optional.

support.title: Nausea prevention and rescue
support.text: Take the prescribed prevention medicines at the planned times and keep rescue treatment available. Tell the team if nausea or constipation is not controlled; do not duplicate steroid or anti-sickness medicines.

support.title: Bowel symptoms
support.text: Report diarrhoea promptly and follow the written rescue plan. Severe symptoms, fever, dehydration or inability to drink need urgent advice.

support.title: Counts and recovery
support.text: White-cell growth-factor injections are prescribed according to individual risk and previous complications. They are not automatically required for every patient or every cycle.

support.title: Cold and nerve symptoms
support.text: Avoid cold exposure as advised after oxaliplatin. Report persistent numbness or difficulty with buttons, walking or everyday tasks before the next dose.

evidence.title: Understanding the evidence
evidence.intro: Ask which evidence matches your cancer, treatment aim and medicines.
evidence.interpretation: The MOSAIC trial found a long-term survival benefit from adding oxaliplatin for people with stage III colon cancer after surgery. The same survival benefit was not established in its stage II group. Metastatic treatment has a different aim and evidence discussion.

chronology_notes.title: Your planned visits
chronology_notes.text: Day 1: oxaliplatin and folinic acid, then fluorouracil bolus and a 22-hour infusion. Day 2: further fluorouracil bolus and a second 22-hour infusion; completion around Day 3. A repeating 14-day cycle. For adjuvant FOLFOX-4, NCCP describes 12 cycles; metastatic treatment continues while suitable.

chronology_notes.title: No guaranteed safe days
chronology_notes.text: An infection, reaction or other urgent problem can occur at any time. The graph does not predict a personal low point.

chronology_notes.title: Care continues
chronology_notes.text: Numbness or tingling can persist after oxaliplatin; tell your team if it affects daily tasks. Ask which medicines to continue and when your next review is planned.

anatomy: Cold-triggered tingling or difficulty with buttons/walking: report.
Pain or ulcers affecting eating or drinking need advice.
New breathing difficulty requires prompt assessment.
New chest pain needs urgent assessment.
Diarrhoea, increased stoma output or dehydration: call early.
Report troublesome skin changes or painful hands/feet.
Fever, shivers or sudden illness: contact oncology immediately.
Pain, swelling, leakage or a loose connection needs immediate advice.

sections.title: Before the first treatment
sections.text: Confirm the aim, likely course length, blood-test arrangements and a working urgent contact number. DPD testing is required before starting the fluoropyrimidine unless already completed.

sections.title: Line and pump arrangements
sections.text: FOLFOX4 has separate fluorouracil infusions over 22 hours on Day 1 and again on Day 2. Confirm both attendance/pump arrangements and the final disconnection; this is not the single 46-hour modified FOLFOX6 schedule.

sections.title: If treatment is delayed
sections.text: Ask the unit to confirm the new treatment and blood-test dates. Re-anchor supportive medicines to the treatment actually given; do not take an extra or catch-up anticancer dose yourself.

sections.title: Getting help between visits
sections.text: Follow your oncology unit’s urgent advice for fever, infection, severe diarrhoea, chest pain or difficulty breathing. Bring your treatment card and current medicines list.
